Reading University Partnership
The 'Students in Schools' scheme places student volunteers in local schools, to help school children raise aspirations and encourage them to continue into higher education. University students develop their personal and employability skills. The scheme has been established for over 20 years and each year several hundred students visit over 40 local schools including primary, secondary and special schools.
We are very pleased to have been working alongside the University of Reading in their 'Students in Schools' scheme since 2016. Over the last 7 years, we have had about 100 students who have come into school to provide additional support in the classroom, this year we already have 10! Typically, we welcome around 25 students each year.
The students are placed in every year group across the school, so children in all classes will be supported by them at some stage. As well as students gaining valuable experience in communicating their knowledge and ideas, they improve their self-confidence. Teachers welcome the extra help and the children enjoy having a new face in the classroom.
Typically, they will make 10 weekly visits of 1 or 2 hours during the Autumn and Spring term due to exams in the Summer term, however many students decide to stay longer. This year we have a student who decided to return for a second year.
With around 150 languages spoken in schools in the area, Reading’s international students are perfectly placed to support children with little-to-no English. This year we are lucky enough to have volunteers who can help our new arrivals from overseas. We have Arabic, Cantonese, Polish, Russian and more working with our children in their native language and helping them learn English.
We have discovered over the years, that both the students and the children benefit. The students learn to be responsible and caring while guiding the children in their learning. For the children it exposes them to different viewpoints and role models, motivating them to think about their own futures. These visits also provide a supportive environment where the students can learn from teaching younger children, helping them grow academically and personally.
The students contribute in lots of ways to support the children. Whether that be assisting in the classroom with various classroom activities such as listening to children read, supporting small group activities or offering one to one support to children who need extra help. The support given to our EAL children is invaluable. We had one child who very rarely spoke, who after working with one of the students, gained the confidence to start communicating with the other children in their class. When the children see the enthusiasm and passion the students have for their chosen field, it inspires them to pursue higher education and they believe that anything is possible.
We look forward to continuing to work alongside the University of Reading.
My name is Alfie and I have been volunteering at Coley Primary School as part of the Students in Schools' Programme for almost two years. I am studying languages at Reading University and I am secretary for the Music Society. I play the saxophone, piano and drums and I also sing. I have been volunteering in year 1 and have really enjoyed getting to know the children and helping them progress. I find it very rewarding. Every day I visit is different and it feels like I am making a difference. The Coley team have made me feel so welcome and I look forward to visiting every week. The children are amazing and their passion for learning is infectious. I love learning alongside the children and sharing my own experiences with them.

Welcome to the Summer SEND Local Offer Newsletter 2026.
Introduction & Latest News
SEND Short breaks, holiday Clubs, Early Years & Childcare
It's all about Summer 2026!
What’s on, events, groups, workshops & clubs
SEND Support – local & national
16-25 Preparation for Adulthood
With the summer holiday approaching we have some fantastic short breaks, activities and support services included in issue 41 of the SEND Local Offer newsletter, it’s a bumper issue again! With a new look email based on parent carer feedback.
Reading SEND Local Offer continues to take the service into the community to support and inform families, attending the Special United (Me2) events, Reading Children’s Festival Forbury Fiesta, Kinship carers groups, attending the Parenting Special Children ethnically diverse group and the Living well with Autism course. Young people and families have really valued our attendance, sharing information about key support and services available in Reading.
Full timetable of support and services offered at the Family Hub is now available through the SEND Local Offer platform, service support from 0-25 are available to families and young people.
Reading SEND Local Offer provides children and young people with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) and their families, information about what support is available in the local area. It helps parents, carers and young people clearly see and access the range of services that they may need. Visit www.readingsendlocaloffer.org Email localoffer@reading.gov.uk Call on 0118 9373777 (option 2), Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm
Many people are family carers and support someone who relies on them to collect shopping, prescriptions and other essential items. You may not identify yourself as a carer because you are firstly a parent, a wife, husband, daughter, son, grandchild, friend or neighbour.
Reading Mencap have produced The Reading Family Carers Card it’s available to carers for FREE and it will identify you as a family carer in order to help shorten the time you might have to spend queueing for a shop, a pharmacy or even a health appointment. It is supported by Reading Borough Council.
Please click on the link below to the Reading Services Guide information page about the Reading Families Carers Card.
https://servicesguide.reading.gov.uk/kb5/reading/directory/advice.page?id=FiM1gU0NzYk
This service was formerly called the Parent Partnership Service. It offers free confidential and impartial advice and support to Reading parents and carers who have children (up to the age of 25) with special educational needs or disability. Therapeutic Support Worker
We are looking to appoint a Therapeutic Support Worker to join our therapeutic team. Then we would like to meet you.

Governors
The Governing Body of Coley Primary School meets termly and is responsible for setting the strategic framework of the school and monitoring its implementation. It acts as a 'critical friend' by holding the Headteacher to account for the educational performance of the school and its pupils. Governors have a general responsibility for the conduct of the school with a view to promoting high standards of education achievement. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Community
approving school targets for student achievement
monitoring the school’s finances
appointing staff
reviewing staff performance and pay

Ideas to help childrendevelop their moral understanding
Supporting your children's moral understanding is essential for their character development. Here are ten ideas to help parents nurture their children's moral development:
Be a Role Model: Demonstrate ethical behavior, kindness, and empathy in your own actions, serving as a positive moral model for your children.
Open Dialogue: Encourage open and non-judgmental discussions about moral dilemmas and ethical choices. Listen to your children's thoughts and concerns.
Read Moral Stories: Share books and stories that present moral dilemmas and discuss the characters' choices and consequences. These stories can prompt meaningful conversations.
Discuss Values: Talk with your children about your family's core values and the importance of honesty, kindness, respect, and other moral principles.
Teach Empathy: Help your children understand and appreciate the feelings and perspectives of others. Encourage them to "walk in someone else's shoes."
Encourage Critical Thinking: Ask open-ended questions that challenge your children to consider different points of view and think critically about moral issues.
Volunteer Together: Participate in volunteer activities or community service projects as a family, emphasising the importance of giving back and helping those in need.
Set Clear Expectations: Establish clear rules and expectations regarding moral behaviour, explaining the consequences of unethical actions.
Problem-Solving: Encourage your children to work through moral dilemmas and ethical choices by discussing potential solutions and their implications.
Reflect on Consequences: Help your children understand that their actions have consequences, both positive and negative. Encourage them to consider the impact of their choices on themselves and others.
Remember that moral development is an ongoing process, and it's important to provide consistent guidance and support as your children grow and encounter increasingly complex moral situations. Be patient and understanding as they navigate the challenges of ethical decision-making.

What You Can Find on the Reading SEND Local Offer - www.readingsendlocaloffer.org
Education & Learning (0–25)
Information on childcare options including Ofsted‑registered provision and childminders offering SEND support. Reading Directory | Early Years & Childcare
Support around Education, Health & Care Plans (EHCPs) and Personal Budgets. Reading Directory | Education, Schools & Services
Information to help you understand schooling, specialist provision and how to access support.
Activities, Clubs & What’s On & Short Breaks
Listings of holiday clubs, events, leisure activities, and inclusive group sessions for children and young people with SEND across Reading. Reading Directory | Special Needs Activities
A wide range of social and community opportunities for young people, including those aged 16+.
SEND Short Breaks Reading Directory | SEND Short Breaks (all ability activities)
SEND Local Offer Newsletter – Spring, Summer and Winter - Reading Directory | SEND Local Offer - Newsletter
Health & Social Care
Information on child and young person health services. Reading Directory | Health & Social Care
Guidance on how to access social care support, especially if your child has complex needs.
Advice for families supporting young people who will eventually move from children to adult services.
Support for Families
Free newsletters and regular information emails to help keep you updated on new groups, services, events and opportunities.
Access to local and national family support organisations. Reading Directory | Special Needs Support
Parent to Parent Support section, created directly in response to parent carer feedback to help families connect with others in similar situations. Reading Directory | Parent to Parent Support
Preparing for the Future Reading Directory | Transition 16-25 - Preparing for Adulthood
Although the Local Offer covers the full 0–25 age range, we also provide dedicated resources for families preparing for the move into adulthood, such as:
Help with post‑16 education, training and employment pathways. Reading Directory | Listings in Education & Training
Preparing for Adulthood resources, including guides and videos explaining the next steps. Reading Directory | Transition - Becoming an adult and preparing for the future
Support services like Reading Mencap’s Preparing for Adulthood Service for young people with Learning Disabilities and Autism (aged 16–25). Reading Directory | Reading Mencap – Preparing for Adulthood Service
The SEND Local Offer Team is here to help with any questions, big or small.
You can contact them at:
localoffer@reading.gov.uk
They are available Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm, and are always happy to support you in finding the right information and services for your child or young person.

Presentation
Today, the Junior Carers visited the hospital for the final time as part of the programme. They were invited into the boardroom, where they gave a presentation about what they had learned during their visits. To celebrate their contributions and commitment, each Junior Carer was presented with a certificate and badge by Dom Hardy, the Chief Operating Officer. As a thank you, the children gave a card to Dom, Sharon, and Maria to express their appreciation to everyone who helped make the Junior Carers Programme possible. Inside the card, they wrote personal reflections about their experiences—some of which you can read below.
A heartfelt thank you to all of our Junior Carers for their commitment, enthusiasm, and contributions throughout the programme. Your compassion and curiosity made each visit meaningful and memorable.
Thank you also to Sharon and Maria for organising such a wide range of engaging experiences and for introducing the children to so many inspiring people.
I am also incredibly grateful to all the adult helpers who supported the monthly visits to the hospital, and to our school’s admin team for their ongoing help behind the scenes. This programme would not have been possible without your time, care, and teamwork.
